title: Cells
intro: All living things are made of cells. Learn the parts of animal and plant cells, special cells, and how cells build tissues and organs.
description: Free KS3 Biology questions with answers on cells: animal and plant cells, the nucleus, cell membrane, chloroplasts and mitochondria, specialised cells, microscopes and levels of organisation. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9.

options: The smallest unit of a living thing
questions.hint: Living things are built from them, like a house is built from bricks.
questions.explain: Cells are the building blocks of all living things. Some living things are just one cell; you are made of trillions.

questions.q: Which part of a cell controls what the cell does?
questions.hint: It's like the cell's control centre.
questions.explain: The nucleus controls the cell. It contains the genetic material (DNA).

options: Controls what goes in and out of the cell
questions.hint: It's a thin layer around the outside of the cell.
questions.explain: The cell membrane controls which substances can move in and out.

questions.q: Where do most chemical reactions in a cell happen?
questions.hint: It's the jelly-like part that fills the cell.
questions.explain: Most reactions happen in the cytoplasm, the jelly-like substance inside the membrane.

questions.hint: Cells need a steady supply of energy.
questions.explain: Mitochondria are where aerobic respiration happens, releasing energy from glucose for the cell to use.

questions.q: Which of these is found in plant cells but **not** in animal cells?
questions.hint: Which part is green and catches light?
questions.explain: Chloroplasts are only in plant cells (and some other living things). Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm and a membrane.

questions.q: What does the **cell wall** do in a plant cell?
options: Supports the cell and keeps its shape
questions.hint: It's tough and made of cellulose.
questions.explain: The cell wall is made of cellulose. It's strong and supports the cell. Animal cells don't have one.

questions.hint: They contain green chlorophyll that absorbs light.
questions.explain: Chloroplasts absorb light to make food (glucose) by photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which three parts do plant cells have that animal cells don't?
options: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole
questions.hint: Animal cells have a nucleus, cytoplasm, membrane and mitochondria too.
questions.explain: Plant cells also have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole filled with cell sap.

questions.q: A root cell from a carrot has no chloroplasts. Why?
options: Roots are underground and get no light
questions.hint: What do chloroplasts need to work?
questions.explain: Roots get no light, so chloroplasts would be no use there. Not every plant cell has them.

questions.q: What is the job of a **red blood cell**?
options: To carry oxygen around the body
questions.hint: It's red because of a substance that grabs oxygen.
questions.explain: Red blood cells carry oxygen from the lungs to every part of the body.

questions.q: Red blood cells have **no nucleus**. How does this help?
options: There's more room to carry oxygen
questions.hint: Think about space inside the cell.
questions.explain: Without a nucleus there's more space for haemoglobin, the substance that carries oxygen.

questions.q: Root hair cells have a long thin part sticking out into the soil. Why?
options: It gives a large surface area to absorb water
It holds the plant up on its own
questions.hint: More surface touching the soil means…
questions.explain: The long thin hair gives a big surface area, so the cell can absorb lots of water and minerals.

questions.q: Which cell is matched with its special feature?
options: Nerve cell: long, to carry messages a long way
Red blood cell: tail, to swim
Sperm cell: chloroplasts, to make food
Root hair cell: no nucleus, for more space
questions.hint: Think about what each cell does.
questions.explain: Nerve cells are long so they can carry electrical messages around the body. Sperm cells have tails; red blood cells have no nucleus.

questions.q: A microscope has an eyepiece lens that magnifies ×10 and an objective lens that magnifies ×40. What is the total magnification?
Which list goes from smallest to largest?
questions.hint: Cells group together to make tissues.
questions.explain: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs work together in organ systems, and organ systems make an organism.

questions.q: The heart is made of muscle tissue, nerve tissue and other tissues. What is the heart?
questions.hint: It's made of several tissues working together.
questions.explain: An organ is made of different tissues working together to do a job.

questions.q: Yeast is a living thing made of just one cell. What is it called?
questions.explain: Unicellular living things are made of one cell. Yeast, many bacteria and amoebas are unicellular.
